source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: 2. clean
entries.text: 2. clean --or, "faultless." weigheth --or, "tries," "judges," implying that they are faulty ( Pr 21:2; 24:12 ).
3. (Compare Margin ). Rely on God for success to your lawful purposes.

entries.heading: 4. for himself
entries.text: 4. for himself --"for its answer," or "purpose," that is, according to God's plan; the wicked are for the day of evil ( Ps 49:5; Jer 17:18 ); sinning and suffering answer to each other, are indissolubly united.
5. (Compare Pr 3:32 ).

entries.heading: 6. By mercy and truth
entries.text: 6. By mercy and truth --that is, God's ( Ps 85:10 ); He effects the atonement, or covering of sin; and the principles of true piety incline men to depart from evil; or, "mercy" and "truth" may be man's, indicative of the gracious tempers which work instrumentally in procuring pardon. purged --expiated (as in Le 16:33; Isa 27:9 , Hebrew ).
7. Persecutions, of course, excepted.
9. (Compare Pr 16:3 ). directeth --establisheth.
10. The last clause depends on the first, expressing the importance of equity in decisions, so authoritative.

entries.heading: 11. are the Lord's . . . his work
entries.text: 11. are the Lord's . . . his work --that is, what He has ordered, and hence should be observed by men.
12. Rulers are rightly expected, by their position, to hate evil; for their power is sustained by righteousness.
13. A specification of the general sentiment of Pr 16:12 .
14. This wrath, so terrible and certain, like messengers of death ( 1Ki 2:25 ), can be appeased by the wise.

entries.heading: 15. light of . . . countenance
entries.text: 15. light of . . . countenance --favor ( Ps 4:6 ). life --preserves it, or gives blessings which make it valuable. the latter rain --fell just before harvest and matured the crop; hence specially valuable ( De 11:14 ).

entries.heading: 17. The highway
entries.text: 17. The highway --A common, plain road represents the habitual course of the righteous in departing from evil. keepeth --observes.
18, 19. (Compare Pr 15:33 ). Haughtiness and pride imply self-confidence which produces carelessness, and hence a fall --literally, "sliding."

entries.heading: 19. divide the spoil
entries.text: 19. divide the spoil --that is, conquer. Avoid the society of the proud ( Jas 4:6 ).

entries.heading: 20. handleth a matter
entries.text: 20. handleth a matter --wisely considers "the word," that is, of God (compare Pr 13:13 ). trusteth --(Compare Ps 2:12; 118:8, 9 ).

entries.heading: 21. wise in heart
entries.text: 21. wise in heart --who rightly consider duty. sweetness of the lips --eloquent discourse, persuades and instructs others.

entries.heading: 22. Understanding
entries.text: 22. Understanding --or, "discretion," is a constant source of blessing ( Pr 13:14 ), benefiting others; but fools' best efforts are folly.
23. The heart is the source of wisdom flowing from the mouth.
24. (Compare Pr 15:26 ). Gentle, kind words, by soothing the mind, give the body health.
25. (Compare Pr 14:2 ).
26. Diligence is a duty due to one's self, for his wants require labor.

entries.heading: 27. ungodly man
entries.text: 27. ungodly man --(Compare Pr 6:12 ). diggeth up evil --labors for it. in his lips . . . fire --His words are calumniating ( Jas 3:6 ).
28. (Compare Pr 6:14; 10:31 ). whisperer --prater, talebearer ( Pr 18:8; 26:20 ).

entries.heading: 29. violent man
entries.text: 29. violent man --or, "man of mischief" ( Pr 3:31 ). enticeth -- ( Pr 1:10 ).

entries.heading: 30. He shutteth his eyes
entries.text: 30. He shutteth his eyes --denoting deep thought ( Ps 64:6 ). moving his lips --or, "biting his lips"--a determined purpose ( Pr 6:13 ).
31. (Compare Pr 20:29 ). if --or, which may be supplied properly, or without it the sense is as in Pr 3:16; 4:10 , that piety is blessed with long life.
32. (Compare Pr 14:29 ). taketh a city --that is, by fighting.
33. Seemingly the most fortuitous events are ordered by God.
